transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

That's completely normal. Siemens (and Bosch, which makes essentially the same machines) dishwashers are designed to leave a small amount of water in the sump, the well under the filter. It keeps the seals and gaskets moist so they don't dry out and crack, and it acts as a barrier against odours coming back up from the drain.

Typically it's somewhere around a cupful sitting in the sump area. You may also notice it's a bit cloudy or has small food particles in it; that's fine too.

**Signs it's not draining properly:
• Water sitting above the filter or covering the floor of the tub
• Dirty water still in the machine at the end of a cycle
• A persistent bad smell
• An error code on the display, especially E24 or E25 (drain problems)
• Cycles taking much longer than usual or stopping mid-programme

If you do see those signs, check:
1. The filter. Twist it out, rinse it under the tap, and make sure the area beneath is clear. It's worth doing every few weeks anyway.
2. The drain hose. Make sure it isn't kinked or crushed behind the machine, especially after a new installation.
3. The connection to your sink waste or waste disposal. If it connects to a new waste disposal unit, the installer must knock out the plastic plug inside the inlet, or nothing will drain.
4. The drain pump cover** (under the filter). Small debris like glass or fruit stones can occasionally jam it.

So if it's just a small pool under the filter and everything else is working fine, your dishwasher is doing exactly what it's supposed to.
